themes_detail.label: Air Quality Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Air quality complaints spiked 1900% THIS WEEK with 5 complaints vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 10.97), suggesting a sudden localized pollution event or industrial emission in Belmont/East Tremont requiring urgent investigation.
evidence: 5 air quality complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly baseline (1900% spike)
Z-score of 10.97 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
No prior context in local news; suggests emerging event rather than long-running issue
reporting_angles: Identify source of air quality spike—industrial facility, construction site, or external pollution event affecting the district
Interview residents about respiratory impact and check with NYC Department of Environmental Protection for air monitoring data
Cross-reference spike timing with DOB permits (370 filed in last 90 days, including demolitions) to determine if construction is culprit

themes_detail.label: Homeless Encampments Surge
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints jumped 638% LAST WEEK with 12 complaints vs. 1.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.27), indicating a significant and sudden increase in visible homelessness across parks and public spaces.
evidence: 12 encampment complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.6 weekly baseline (638% spike)
Z-score of 6.27 indicates statistically severe deviation
Park Rules violations also up 700% LAST WEEK (3 complaints vs. 0.4 avg), suggesting encampments are concentrating in parks
reporting_angles: Map where encampments are concentrated (parks mentioned in Park Rules complaints) and interview homeless individuals about housing barriers
Contact NYC Department of Homeless Services to determine if recent policy changes or shelter capacity issues drove migration to this district
Investigate community board's repeated funding requests for senior centers and social services—potential unmet need for vulnerable populations

themes_detail.label: Construction & Plumbing Spike
themes_detail.summary: General Construction/Plumbing complaints surged 200% LAST WEEK with 21 complaints vs. 7.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.29), coinciding with 370 DOB permits filed in last 90 days and suggesting widespread building work disruption.
evidence: 21 construction/plumbing complaints LAST WEEK vs. 7.0 weekly baseline (200% spike)
Z-score of 5.29 indicates high statistical significance
370 total DOB permits filed in last 90 days (185 alterations, 128 new buildings, 15 demolitions) suggests active construction across district
reporting_angles: Cross-reference highest-complaint neighborhoods with DOB permit map to identify which projects are generating complaints
Interview residents and property managers about noise, debris, and disruption from construction activity
Investigate whether permits are being filed without adequate community notice or whether contractors are violating work-hour restrictions

themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Complaints
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints jumped 300% 2 WEEKS AGO with 4 complaints vs. 1.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.24), suggesting emerging traffic or unsafe driving concerns related to Uber/Lyft activity.
evidence: 4 for-hire vehicle complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 1.0 weekly baseline (300% spike)
Z-score of 4.24 indicates statistical significance, though already 1-2 weeks old
Community board budget requests include 'other transportation infrastructure requests,' suggesting persistent transit/traffic concerns
reporting_angles: Determine nature of complaints—unsafe driving, double-parking, or congestion caused by for-hire vehicle pickup/dropoff zones
Interview residents and business owners about impact of Uber/Lyft congestion on neighborhood streets
Cross-reference with illegal parking complaints (1,074 in 90 days) to assess if for-hire vehicles are contributing to parking crisis
